parsed.explanation: The combined regime is high-risk but not catastrophic: there is no general criminalisation of trans identity or execution pathway. Yet traveller-facing exposures are serious. National binary-sex passport/visa rules, halted X markers, refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility can strand or exclude. The division backs sex-segregated facilities, bans under-19 care, and documents birth-sex custody placement with sexual assault and dismissed failure-to-protect claims; national immigration custody abuse is also documented. National hate-crime coverage, marriage recognition, local ordinances and some injunctions are real but mostly climate or post-harm recourse, not operative border, facility or custody protections.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex passport/visa rules; X marker halted; entry cable requires refusal or additional evidence where sex is doubted, with possible permanent fraud ineligibility; reports of confiscated/blocked passports and stranded travellers. Division EO defines sex by birth, though visitors use home passports.
entry_documents.protection: Passport restrictions are challenged in national court and some related orders are enjoined; a legal-aid FAQ exists; existing national X passports remain valid until expiry. No documented visitor-facing waiver or reliable border remedy.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign passport/visa mismatch can trigger secondary screening, refusal, fraud investigation or detention; local document rules do not directly govern foreign passports but signal official hostility.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men. The division housed a trans woman by birth sex with a male sex offender who assaulted her; her claims were dismissed. National corrections practices include conversion-style treatment.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity but does not address custody; no working custody remedy is documented, and the division case was dismissed.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry fraud suspicion or local arrest can move a traveller into immigration or local custody, where birth-sex placement and documented abuse follow.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The division EO defines sex at birth and backs single-sex bathrooms and changing rooms in state agencies; national maps show many facility bans and some criminal trespass provisions. No division arrest or enforcement provision is documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No state-wide gender-identity public-accommodation law; one city ordinance exists; national maps note some states lack bans. National law does not override local facility practice on this record.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Government buildings and facilities are the main exposure; private settings are mostly uncovered, and enforcement in the division is uncertain.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for under-19 is banned and was upheld by the state supreme court; a visitor cannot obtain it for a minor in their care. National proposed insurance restrictions target under-18 care. Adult care access is not documented.
care_services.protection: No documented visitor or minor exception; local ordinances do not restore care; some national orders are enjoined, but not this state ban.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor faces denial of care; adult emergency-care access is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; a justice reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; the division EO frames biological sex. The official climate is hostile to trans visibility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; some national measures are enjoined; no documented prosecution of trans travellers for ideology.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetoric raises police suspicion and outing risk but no direct traveller prosecution is documented; it interacts with border screening and custody.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-19 care ban; athletics ban; school rules require hormone/surgery evidence; national EO directs investigation of teachers who facilitate social transition. A trans minor visitor cannot access care, and a parent cannot obtain it.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented visitor exception; marriage/adoption recognition is irrelevant to care; local ordinances do not address minors' care.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor meets care denial and hostile school/athletics rules; custody or guardianship risk is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state/province trans violence statistics are in the dossier; the state hate-crime law omits gender identity; the custody record shows institutional failure. National counterterrorism rhetoric may embolden hostility.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; the state hate-crime law has been applied to association bias; one city anti-discrimination ordinance and national fair-housing enforcement exist.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Bias crime can be charged nationally, but local recourse is uneven; no documented pattern of visitor-targeted violence is presented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport policy remains in effect; the civil-liberties suit is pending; custody claims were dismissed; the care ban was upheld; facility enforcement is unclear; there is no state-wide gender-identity anti-discrimination law.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National courts have blocked some orders; national hate-crime and fair-housing enforcement exist; local ordinances and a legal-aid FAQ exist; marriage and adoption are settled.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are partial and contested; travellers must verify current national measures; no reliable remedy is documented for border refusal or custody harm.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A treats severe multi-year imprisonment as the standard outcome for identity misrepresentation, with possible capital exposure. This dossier has no general criminalisation or execution pathway for trans status; entry refusal, fraud ineligibility and custody abuse are serious but not that automatic imprisonment regime. It rates above 0.15-A.

0.35-A documents administrative exclusion and paper confiscation without detention. This dossier adds documented birth-sex custody harm, immigration-custody abuse, a minor care ban and possible permanent fraud ineligibility, so it sits below 0.35-A.

0.55-B has a functioning protection that eventually corrects an administrative delay. Here remedies are contested or dismissed, and the division custody case shows no effective protection after harm. This is materially lower than 0.55-B.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is high-risk but not catastrophic. The harshest operative features are traveller-facing: binary-sex document screening with refusal or fraud consequences, state-backed sex-segregated facilities, birth-sex custody with documented assault and no remedy, under-19 care denial, and official counterterrorism rhetoric. National hate-crime coverage, marriage recognition, local ordinances and court injunctions are real but mostly climate or post-harm recourse; they do not offset border, facility or custody exposure. A short-stay adult using a consistent foreign passport may avoid the worst, but if outed at a checkpoint, facility or arrest, the documented system can refuse entry, strand, or place them in unsafe custody. Minors and guardians face additional care denial.
